messages.subject: User friendly shiny wrapper idea
messages.subject_clean: User friendly shiny wrapper idea
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I'm new here so please let me know if there are any problems with this post.

I sat down a couple weeks ago and wrote a wrapper for auto-generating shiny apps. The original goal was to leverage the power of shiny in a way that a beginner R user (or a lazy advanced user) can interactively tweak plotting parameters. Analogous in purpose (I think) to qplot for ggplot2, this would be a gateway to working with shiny. The apps can be generated from pre-existing scripts with minimal additional coding

I only spent a day on it, so I'm certain that it is very buggy and full of compatibility issues. I just thought I should post it here. It would be great if similar functionality could be incorporated directly into the shiny package.

You can read more about it on the git repository here: https://github.com/cfhammill/friendlyShiny

I'd love to hear any thoughts you all may have on this idea.

Cheers,

Chris

messages.subject: leaflet-shiny: changing initalTileLayer
messages.subject_clean: leaflet-shiny: changing initalTileLayer
messages.body_plain: Hi, First of all this is a great package, it's easy to grab the map bounds and zoom level, among other features. However, I am having difficulty dynamically changing the initialTileLayer using shiny-leaflet. I have created a minimal example using two different initialTileLayer's. It seems to require two corresponding maps in server.R. Here is the ui.R: library(shiny);library(leaflet) shinyServer(function(input, output, session) { output$map1 <- reactive(TRUE) map1 <- createLeafletMap(session, "map1") output$map2 <- reactive(TRUE) map2 <- createLeafletMap(session, "map2") }) It also requires a styles.css in the same directory as server.R and ui.R: div.outer { position: fixed; top: 41px; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; overflow: hidden; padding: 0; } Here's the ui.R: library(shiny);library(leaflet) shinyUI(navbarPage("Switch Map", tabPanel("Map", conditionalPanel( condition = "input.bmappick == 'MapQuestOpen.Aerial'", div(class="outer",tags$head(includeCSS("styles.css")), leafletMap("map1", "100%", "100%", initialTileLayer = "http://oatile3.mqcdn.com/tiles/1.0.0/sat/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg ", initialTileLayerAttribution = HTML('Tiles Courtesy of MapQuest — Portions Courtesy NASA/JPL-Caltech and U.S. Depart. of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency'), options=list(center = c(40, -98.85),zoom = 5)))), conditionalPanel( condition = "input.bmappick == 'OpenStreetMap'", div(class="outer",tags$head(includeCSS("styles.css")), leafletMap("map2", "100%", "100%", initialTileLayer = "http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png ", initialTileLayerAttribution = HTML('Tiles Courtesy of OpenStreetMap contributors, CC-BY-SA'), options=list(center = c(40, -98.85),zoom = 5))) ), absolutePanel(top = 60, left = "auto", right = 20, bottom = "auto", selectInput("bmappick", "Background Map",c("OpenStreetMap" = 'OpenStreetMap', "MapQuestOpen.Aerial"= 'MapQuestOpen.Aerial'),selected = c("OpenStreetMap")))) )) The background map that is not selected first by default through "bmappick" never fills the entire screen and appears to be a single tile. Is there a way to do this? I greatly appreciate any help. I know leaflet has the ability to add a "layers control" to the map (http://leafletjs.com/examples/layers-control.html) but I don't see a reference to control.layers in the bindings (https://github.com/jcheng5/leaflet-shiny/blob/4cf37eb81342925bb3537c1678546d50b82f54f7/inst/www/binding.js). I'm new to Javascript so I could be totally missing something, and I don't need to use Leaflet directly for this. Regards, Chris P.S. to install leaflet-shiny: if (!require(devtools)) install.packages('devtools') devtools::install_github('leaflet-shiny', 'jcheng5')

Hi,

one way is to use renderUI like this:

runApp(list(
  ui = fluidPage(

    fluidRow(
      column(3,
             uiOutput("RenderSliders")
      )
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$RenderSliders <- renderUI({

      Animals     <- c("cat","dog","fish","cow")
      NrOfAnimals <- length(Animals)

      L <- vector("list",length = NrOfAnimals)

      for(i in 1:NrOfAnimals){

        L[[i]]  <- fluidRow(column(1,checkboxInput(paste0("x",i) ,NULL,TRUE)),
                            column(2,Animals[i]),
                            column(4,numericInput(paste0("y",i) , NULL, value = i, min = 0, max = 10, step = 1)))
      }

      return(L)

    })

  }
))

best Herman

messages.body_plain: My workaround in case somebody else runs into this. ui.R: library(shiny);library(leaflet) shinyUI(navbarPage("Switch Map", tabPanel("Map", div(class="outer",tags$head(includeCSS("styles.css")), htmlOutput("mapp",inline=TRUE)), absolutePanel(top = 60, left = "auto", right = 20, bottom = "auto", selectInput("mapPick", "Background Map",c("OpenStreetMap" = "http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png ", "MapQuestOpen.Aerial"= "http://oatile3.mqcdn.com/tiles/1.0.0/sat/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg "), selected = c("http://oatile3.mqcdn.com/tiles/1.0.0/sat/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg ")))))) server.R: library(shiny);library(leaflet) shinyServer(function(input, output, session) { output$map1 <- reactive(TRUE) map1 <- createLeafletMap(session, "map") output$mapp <- renderUI({ input$mapPick isolate({ leafletMap("map", "100%", "100%", initialTileLayer = input$mapPick, initialTileLayerAttribution = HTML('Fix This Later'), options=list(center = center(),zoom = zoom())) }) }) zoom <- reactive({ ifelse(is.null(input$map_zoom),5,input$map_zoom) }) center <- reactive({ if(is.null(input$map_bounds)) { c(40, -98.85) } else { map_bounds <- input$map_bounds c((map_bounds$north + map_bounds$south)/2.0,(map_bounds$east + map_bounds$west)/2.0) } }) }) On Sunday, August 3, 2014 10:48:02 PM UTC-5, Chris Holcomb wrote: > Hi, > > First of all this is a great package, it's easy to grab the map bounds and zoom level, among other features. However, I am having difficulty dynamically changing the initialTileLayer using shiny-leaflet. > > I have created a minimal example using two different initialTileLayer's. It seems to require two corresponding maps in server.R. Here is the ui.R: > > library(shiny);library(leaflet) > shinyServer(function(input, output, session) { > output$map1 <- reactive(TRUE) > map1 <- createLeafletMap(session, "map1") > output$map2 <- reactive(TRUE) > map2 <- createLeafletMap(session, "map2") > }) > > It also requires a styles.css in the same directory as server.R and ui.R: > > div.outer { > position: fixed; > top: 41px; > left: 0; > right: 0; > bottom: 0; > overflow: hidden; > padding: 0; > } > > Here's the ui.R: > > library(shiny);library(leaflet) > shinyUI(navbarPage("Switch Map", > tabPanel("Map", > conditionalPanel( > condition = "input.bmappick == 'MapQuestOpen.Aerial'", > div(class="outer",tags$head(includeCSS("styles.css")), > leafletMap("map1", "100%", "100%", > initialTileLayer = "http://oatile3.mqcdn.com/tiles/1.0.0/sat/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg ", > initialTileLayerAttribution = > HTML('Tiles Courtesy of MapQuest — > Portions Courtesy NASA/JPL-Caltech and U.S. Depart. of Agriculture, Farm Service Agency'), > options=list(center = c(40, -98.85),zoom = 5)))), > conditionalPanel( > condition = "input.bmappick == 'OpenStreetMap'", > div(class="outer",tags$head(includeCSS("styles.css")), > leafletMap("map2", "100%", "100%", > initialTileLayer = "http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png ", > initialTileLayerAttribution = > HTML('Tiles Courtesy of OpenStreetMap > contributors, CC-BY-SA'), > options=list(center = c(40, -98.85),zoom = 5))) > ), > absolutePanel(top = 60, left = "auto", right = 20, bottom = "auto", > selectInput("bmappick", "Background Map",c("OpenStreetMap" = 'OpenStreetMap', > "MapQuestOpen.Aerial"= 'MapQuestOpen.Aerial'),selected = c("OpenStreetMap")))) )) > > The background map that is not selected first by default through "bmappick" never fills the entire screen and appears to be a single tile. Is there a way to do this? I made a demo of a clickable plot for BioC2014 conference, you can adapt the code here: https://github.com/mikelove/shinyMA

messages.subject_clean: Accessing variables in server.R from UI.R
messages.body_plain:
Ravi,

A couple of examples in the Shiny Gallery show this functionality:

http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/update-input-demo.html
http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/dynamic-ui.html

and also documentations on checkboxGroupInput and updateCheckboxGroupInput functions are helpful.

But a very short example, somewhat based on your code, is here:

server.R

library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  observe({
    c_num <- input$control_num
    cb_options <- list()
    cb_options[[paste("Option1", "A")]] <- paste0("optionA")
    cb_options[[paste("Option2", "B")]] <- paste0("optionB")
    cb_options[[paste("Option3", "C")]] <- paste0("optionC")
    updateCheckboxGroupInput(session, "Values", choices = cb_options,
                             selected = paste0("optionA"))
  })

  output$option <- renderText({
    input$Values
  })
})

ui.R

library(shiny)
shinyUI(fluidPage(

  tabPanel("Choose values",
           titlePanel("Click on the values"),
           fluidRow(
             column(width = 3,
                    tags$hr(),
                    checkboxGroupInput("Values",
                                       label = h3("Click on Values"),

                                       choices =c("A", "B", "C"),
                                       selected="A")
             )
           )
  ),
  tabPanel("output", verbatimTextOutput("option"))
))

You can see that in server.R, a static list of cb_options is created. This is where you want to read values from excel and assign to the list.

Hope this helps,
Fereshteh

messages.body_plain:
Ok .... for some strange reason , devtools wasn't downloading the master.zip to the tempdir() ...

Here is what I did ..

1) download the file using wget , wget https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/archive/master.zip
2) copy it to the directory listed when I run tempdir()
3) run the devtools::install_github("rstudio/rmarkdown")
4) Profit!

And it works ... Perhaps because I have both shiny-server and rstudio-server both on the same server? No idea. But hope it gives another way of solving the issue to some other people who are also facing the same issue.

```{r opts.label = 'shiny'}
slidifyUI(
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput('n',
                'Tamanho da população',
               min = 2,
               max = 500,
               value = 3),

    checkboxInput("showcurve", "Mostrar curva", FALSE)
  ),
  mainPanel(
#tags$div(id = 'hist',class='shiny-html-output nvd3 rChart')
tags$div(id = 'hist', class='shiny-plot-output')
  )
)
```

app1.R

require(fdth)

output$hist <- renderPlot({
  tab = fdt(rnorm(input$n,
                  1.75,
                  0.1))
  n1 <- plot(tab,
             ylab = 'Frequência absoluta',
             xlab = 'Intervalo de classes')
  n1$set(dom = 'hist', width = 600)
  n1
})

Thank's!

The table tab is the default view, so when the user clicks on the actionButton titled "Graph" they currently then have to click on the "Graph" tab to view the results. I would like to have the actionButton automatically change focus to the Graph tab, but I am unable to find any documentation on how to access the output from the actionButton for the purpose.

Here's what I have:

library(shiny)

# Define the overall UI
shinyUI(fluidPage(
    titlePanel("A.inornata gene expression during tail regeneration"),

    sidebarPanel(
        selectInput(inputId="measure", label="Select measurement:",
              choices = c("CPM by time point", "RPKM by time point", "CPM by sample", "RPKM by sample")),
    textInput(inputId="comp", label="Enter contig to graph:", value=""),
    helpText("To graph expression, enter the gene name and description here, then click the 'graph' button."),
    actionButton(inputId="graph.button", label="Graph", icon=NULL)

),#end sidepanel

   mainPanel(
       tabsetPanel(id="tabs",
       tabPanel(title="Table", value="panel1", dataTableOutput(outputId="table")),
       tabPanel(title="Graph", value="panel2", plotOutput("graph")))

           )
       ))

server.R

    observe({
        #this doesn't even begin to work
         if input$graph.button == TRUE {
            updateTabsetPanel(session, "tabs", selected = "panel2")
        } else {
            updateTabsetPanel(session, "tabs", selected = "panel1")
        }
    })

I know it's way off, thanks in advance for any help!

messages.subject: Re: server-side selectizeInput doesn't work properly
messages.subject_clean: server-side selectizeInput doesn't work properly
messages.body_plain:
So, after some time, I finally figured it out.

You have to make a data frame, with two columns with names: value and label and then pass it to selectizeInput.
In this case you can search in the selectizeInput with labels and when you select them, they will return values.

This easy example will explain everything:

#### server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  d <- c("moderate 1","moderate 2","moderate 3","bad 1","bad 2","good 1","good 2","good 3")
  data <- data.frame(value=d, label=d)
  updateSelectizeInput(session, 'group', choices = data, server = TRUE)

  output$values <- renderText({
    input$group
  })
})

##### ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  selectizeInput('group', NULL, NULL, multiple = TRUE),
  uiOutput("values")
))

Obviously `lineprof` would need minor modifications, but it seems worthwhile to me to do this.

messages.subject_clean: Unexpected double call of renderPlot; conditionalPanel problem?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I noticed in some examples of mine that my mainplot if called twice (with the same input parameter) when I made a choice in a selectInput (one call would have been ok). This behaviour appreared only with the shiny server and not under R Studio. I tried to build a minimal example, but with it everything worked well. I added more and more code until the problem again appeared.

ui.R:
...
mmstat.getDatasets("USCRIME", "CARS", "DECATHLON")
...
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Dotplot with location parameters"),

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput(inputId ="method",
                  label   = "Select a Dotplot type",
                  choices = c("overplot", "jitter", "stack")
      ),

      HTML('<hr>'),
      selectInput("dataset",
                  label   = "Select a data set and a variable",
                  choices = mmstat$datachoices)

      # add as many panels as you have datasets
      mmstat$dataset[[1]]$panel,
      mmstat$dataset[[2]]$panel,
      mmstat$dataset[[3]]$panel
      ),

    mainPanel(plotOutput("distPlot"))),

    htmlOutput("logText")
))

With mmstat.getDatasets I read in three dataset between the user can choose. Additionally I create also contionalPanels such that user can choose only between variables from the current data set. The panels are stored in the global list mmstat. If I include them into ui.R then the double call sometimes appears during a long press of an choice in the first selectInput. Question: Is the definition from conditionalPanel outside shinyUI a problem?

Thanks in advance

Sigbert

In ui.R, you can wrap your xxxOutput with a div, specify a size, and specify overflow scrolling.

Example vertical scroll:

div(style='height:600px; overflow-y: scroll',
   tableOutput("view")
)

Example scroll both directions:

div(style='height:600px; width:300px; overflow: scroll',
   tableOutput("view")
)

messages.body_plain:
See if this helps.

########### server.R

library(shiny)
library(quantmod)

data <- getSymbols('AAPL')
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  # create a reactive variable
  rvals <- reactiveValues(dataReady = 0)

  values <- reactive({

    invalidateLater(input$delay * 1000, session)
    Sys.sleep(2) # This sleep represents some intensive calculation that takes a few seconds to crunch through
    startbar <- sample(1:1000,1)

    # done with computations, ready to plot, so trigger a reactive variable
    # the rval must be in isolate() to avoid an infinite loop!
    # it is scoped so that we don't need the <<- assignment
    isolate(rvals$dataReady <- rvals$dataReady + 1)

    res <<- AAPL[startbar:(startbar + 250),]
    res
  })

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    y <- values() # need this for updating in plot to work...
    chart_Series(res)
  })

  output$distPlot2 <- renderPlot({
    #invalidateLater(input$delay * 1000, session)
    rvals$dataReady #set dependency
    chart_Series(res)
  })

})

We have percentage data and we want to show the whole possible range of 0-100 instead of the narrower range of observed values. Here is the relevant code:

library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
...

    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Plot", uiOutput("plot_ui"),
               ggvisOutput("plot"), value="plot"),
    )
  )
))

require(ggvis)
require(dplyr)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  data <- reactive({
    ...
    df
  })

  gv <- reactive({
    data <- data()
      if(is.null(input$county)){
        df <- subset(data, County=="MA")

        df %>% ggvis(~Year, ~Crude.Rate) %>%
          add_axis("y", title="Crude Rate",
                   ticks=11,
                   values=seq(0,100, 10),
                   properties = axis_props(
                     labels = list(
                       fontSize=12),
                     title = list(fontSize=14))) %>%
          add_axis("x", title="Year", format="####") %>%
          layer_points() %>%
          layer_lines() %>%
          add_tooltip(function(df) paste(df$Crude.Rate, ", ", df$Year))
  })
   gv %>% bind_shiny("plot", "plot_ui")
})

Steve

messages.subject: Re: [upload/input] Is there a way to select a directory rather than individual files?
messages.subject_clean: [upload/input] Is there a way to select a directory rather than individual files?
messages.body_plain:
Here's some code that might help

This first bit is a reactive expression for the server side that randomly chooses a sub directory when the user clicks an action button. The directories are named with different years (2009 to 2013), different month-day values, and an ID number (OUID). The expression picks a folder, extracts the ID and month-day value, and then outputs this stuff and the file name as a list. Perhaps you could modify this so that it uses an input widget to designate a folder among those available instead of just setting the random seed. You can call this expression in anything you want to update when the user picks a file.

  newdeal <- reactive({
    set.seed(input$action)
    order <- sample(2009:2013, 5, replace = F)
    thefolder <- sample(1:length(allfolders),1)
    thefolder <- allfolders[thefolder]
    OUID <- substr(thefolder, 1, 3)
    moday <- substr(thefolder, 9, 12)
         newstuff <- list(OUID, moday, thefolder)
    return(newstuff)
  }).

messages.body_plain:
Ross,

I am not an export in Apache, and also not familiar with how network and firewall is setup, but from what you have described it seems that ports 3838 and 4151 are not always blocked, but they get blocked by the proxy on port 8080. Would be good to know how the proxy is configured that is blocking other ports.

Fereshteh

messages.subject: Please help us test DataTables 1.10.2
messages.subject_clean: Please help us test DataTables 1.10.2
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

We just integrated the new version of the DataTables library (1.10.2)
into the development version of shiny. Due to the tremendous changes
in parameter names from DataTables 1.9.x to 1.10.x, we want to make
sure DataTables 1.10.2 still works reasonably well in shiny. If you
are interested in testing the development version, please install it
via:

  if (!require("devtools")) install.packages("devtools")
  devtools::install_github(c("rstudio/htmltools", "rstudio/shiny"))

A guide for upgrading parameter names from DT 1.9.x to 1.10.x is here:
https://datatables.net/upgrade/1.10-convert We have tried to
automatically correct some of the old parameter names in shiny, but
this automatic correction certainly won't work for all use cases,
especially if you have deeply customized your DataTables using
complicated JavaScript options. You can see
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/commit/6f2a5618 for examples
of converting DT 1.9 names to 1.10 names.

Please let us know if you have any comments or questions. Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: renderDataTable - Help
messages.subject_clean: renderDataTable - Help
messages.body_plain:
That is because your DataTable options depends on the checkboxes,
which is not reflected in your code. To reflect the dependency, you
have to return the options via a function. Here is an example using
DataTables 1.10.2 (
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/-0u-wTnq_lA ):

renderDataTable(..., options = function() {
  list(pageLength = 10, ...,
       columnDefs = list(list(targets = seq_along(input$show_vars) -
1, searchable = FALSE))
})

It may take a while to understand it. It seems you want to disable the
search boxes for the first n -1 columns where n is the number of the
data. In this case, n = length(input$show_vars) + 1 (+1 because of the
Species column), so basically you want to disable the columns
1:length(input$show_vars), which I wrote as
seq_along(input$show_vars). Then the -1 part is due to JavaScript
indices start from 0 instead of 1, e.g. column 0 means the first
column, column 1 is the second, and so on.

Regards,
Yihui

Our main organization's IT folks had told us this was already done, but we are not sure given our experience.  Is there an alternative solution? Are there any other diagnostic steps you would suggest that might help us focus in on the right things?

As far as creating the data in a suitable format for leaflet-shiny, I couldn't quickly get it to work but I'm fairly confident you can do it without "fortify". Perhaps convert to SpatialPolygonsDataFrame or geojson and parse that. I suspect my attempt failed for this data because some are multipolygons and shiny-leaflet does not support those. You would need to combine them into polygons or keep them separate and tie together those id's to their proper information. messages.body_plain:
yes, I can match the hover event with the ID's I want. For example, when I hover on Michigan.North, I can manage to return both Michigan.North and Michigan.South.
But there are problems when I try to add both Michigan.North and Michigan.South to the map and highlight them.

Here is the code for my app:
server.R:

library(leaflet)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(maps)
library(ggplot2)

rm(list = ls())
states <- map("state", plot=FALSE, fill=TRUE)
states$names <- gsub(':', '.', states$names )
statesDF <- fortify(states, region = 'id')
eachState <- split(statesDF, statesDF$region)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  map <- createLeafletMap(session, "map")
  observe({if (is.null(input$map_click)) {
      return()
    }
  })

  # session$onFlushed is necessary to delay the drawing of the polygons until
  # after the map is created
  session$onFlushed(once= T, function() {
    map$addPolygon(states$y, states$x, states$names,
      lapply(brewer.pal(7, "Set1"), function(x) {
        list(fillColor = x)
      }),
      list(fill=T, fillColor="#800026", fillOpacity=.6,
        stroke=TRUE, opacity=1, color="white", weight=1.5, dashArray = '3'
      )
    )
  })

  observe({
    # mouseover event (eventOver)
    # when the pointer is over a state, highlight that state and
    # show information. layerID of addPolygon should be set as "sameID"
    # or any other name, so that the previou states are not highlighted.

    # when the highlighted state polygon is added, the eventOver$id will be
    # updated to 's' (this is weird!). In order to avoid capturing the
    # highlited state, set return() when eventOver$id == 's'.
    eventOver <- input$map_shape_mouseover
    if (is.null(eventOver)||eventOver$id == 's') {
      return()
    }

    stateOver <- eachState[[eventOver$id]]
    map$addPolygon(stateOver$lat, stateOver$long, 'sameID')
    output$eventOverInfo <- renderPrint({(eventOver$id)})
  })
})

ui.R:
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  textOutput('eventOverInfo'),

  # create a div to contain leaflet Map, so that I can use percentage to
  # control the heigth of the map
  # or else the heigth must be absolute px value (e.g. 500)
  div(class = 'mapContainer',
    leafletMap(
      "map", width = "100%", height = "100%",
      initialTileLayer = "http://{s}.tiles.mapbox.com/v3/jianhua1122.j5f28jda <http://tiles.mapbox.com/v3/jianhua1122.j5f28jda>
      /{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
      initialTileLayerAttribution = NULL,
      options=list(
        center = c(40, -98.85),
        zoom = 4)
    )
  ),

  tags$head(tags$style("
    .mapContainer {
      position: fixed;
      top: 50px;
      left: 0;
      right: 0;
      bottom: 0;
      overflow: hidden;
      padding: 0;
    }
  "))
))

As you can see from the code, in order to avoid highlighting the previous states hovered over, the ID for the highlighted polygons should be set as "sameID". In this way, only the current state being hovered is highlighted.
When the polygon has two parts, they can't share the "sameID". As a result, only the last part can be highlighted.

This problem may be solved by highlighting the matched IDs directly, instead of adding the highlighted polygons as a new layer. But I can't find any function to highlight a polygong in leaflet. Maybe it is available in javascript code.

Thanks for any input.

Jianhua

messages.subject: Re: Observer evaluation too eager?
messages.subject_clean: Observer evaluation too eager?
messages.body_plain:
This is the intended behavior and David's suggestion is the idiom we recommend. Observers (and reactive expressions for that matter) can't know what their dependencies are without running.

I understand that this isn't the most intuitive behavior if you're expecting an observer to work like an "event handler" in most other languages or UI frameworks; we have a pull request that's been open forever that adds a facade over observer() to provide an API that's more event handler-like.

This is the basic idiom for event handlers in Shiny:

observe({
  if (input$button == 0) return()  # or however else you detect the starting state

  isolate({
    # Your event handling logic here
  })
})

See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/isolation.html for more details.

messages.subject: Reactivity and directory watching
messages.subject_clean: Reactivity and directory watching
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm building a tool that takes files in a directory, processes them and output results in another directory (see *note*). The source directory and processing are getting bigger and instead of processing everything every time, I would like to watch for changes in the source directory and only process what changed. I know Hadley faced a similar pb with rsmith https://github.com/hadley/rsmith and solved it using shiny reactive "plumbing". I've read the source and I am still not sure how.

The first step is finding which files change to process them. I can do this with a `reactivePoll` on the files size and modification time (in `checkFunc`) but in `valueFunc` I actually have to find again which files changed (because I don't have access to the output of `checkFunc`) and process only those. I'm not sure how that is different from an infinite `while` loop that does (pseudocode)
  old = file.info <http://file.info>(dir)
  while ( 0 < 1)
    new = file.info <http://file.info>(dir)
    dif = setdiff(new, old)
    process(dif)
    old = new
    sleep(1)
I actually feels less efficient even, since the differences between old and new have to be computed twice.
In Hadley's rsmith, each file is actually "reactive" and this is then put in a higher level `reactivePoll`... but I must admit I don't really follow how the data flows in this code (watch() in https://github.com/hadley/rsmith/blob/master/R/output.R and reactive_file_with_metadata() in https://github.com/hadley/rsmith/blob/master/R/rsmith-file.R).

The second step is probably more tricky. Let us say I have a csv data file which is read by an R file which outputs something. I would like the R process to be run again if the _data_ file changes (with the loop above, it would be run only if the R file itself changes). I am guessing that if I put the data reading in a reactive function and the data processing in another reactive function, I could get the events to be chained. But everything would still start from a request for the output of the processing (which then propagates down). I am not sure how to initiate this from the bottom, when the data changes.

I would welcome any pointers. I think this kind of problem is a very nice and broad application for the reactive principles implemented in shiny, even though it is more remote from the core functionality of serving webapps.

Thanks in advance. Sincerely,

*note* In my case it is a static website generator https://github.com/jiho/yssr, but there are many other use cases: source directory of data files and visualisation scripts which produce output graphs, source directory of raw data which gets processed into cleaned data etc.

messages.subject: Re: using shiny to map zip codes as a choropleth?
messages.subject_clean: using shiny to map zip codes as a choropleth?
messages.body_plain:
First, with the original question, a better way to get a file suitable file for leaflet-shiny. Here's how you can parse a SpatialDataFrame. NOTE: Before you do this you'll need to convert it to Polygons from MultiPolygons and simplify the files. I noticed that the maps in the maps package have far fewer lat-longs than raw CENSUS shapefiles read into SpatialDataFrames. I highly recommend PostGIS, specifically ST_Simplify, ST_GeometryN, ST_Union, ST_Dump, ST_MakeValid, and ST_SnapToGrid. Try this out on ZCTAs and let us know how it goes, it takes very little time on counties that have been previously simplified, but I'm unsure about ZCTAs.

library(sp);library(maptools);library(maps)
getMap  <- function(sdf) {
  getLatLongs <- function(polygon) {
    currentPolygon <- slot(polygon,"Polygons")
    # only single Polygons
    x <- slot(currentPolygon[[1]],"coords")[,1]
    y <- slot(currentPolygon[[1]],"coords")[,2]
    return(list("x"=c(x,NA),"y"=c(y,NA)))
  }
  allLatLongs <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, lapply(slot(sdf, "polygons"), function(x) getLatLongs(x)))
  # may need to change NAME to what you want to display
  names <- as.vector(slot(sdf,"data")$NAME)
  # there's probably a better way to handle the inserted NAs for calculating range
  range <- c(range(allLatLongs$x[!is.na <http://is.na>(allLatLongs$x)]),range(allLatLongs$y[!is.na <http://is.na>(allLatLongs$y)]))
  prepped <- list("x"=allLatLongs$x,"y"=allLatLongs$y,"range"=range,"names"=names)
  attr(prepped , "class") <- "map"
  return(prepped)
}
# set Proj4 to correct string via spatialreference.org <http://spatialreference.org> or prj2epsg.org <http://prj2epsg.org>'s API + PostGIS's spatial_ref_sys
sdfStates <- readShapeSpatial('tl_2013_us_state.shp',proj4string = CRS(Proj4))
saveRDS(getMap(sdfStates),'states.rds')

Now what you'll also really want to do to make the following example complete is to calculate the range of each of the polygons so you can later subset the displayed polygons to the polygons within the viewable map. I have not done this yet, but one method would be to calculate bounds for each polygon and save that as a separate data.frame. Then you would calculate a buffer around input$map_bounds, subset the aforementioned data.frame and let the program reactively run the getMap function, which I imagine will be quick for smaller numbers of polygons. A cleaner route would be to let R access the simplied polygons loaded in PostGIS and conduct a ST_Intersects join with a buffered geometry defined by input$map_bounds. If someone gets around to this, please let me know how fast it is for huge sets of polygons like the ZCTAs.

Anyways, this example shows you how to do the changing polygons by input$map_zoom part:

ui.R
library(shiny);library(leaflet)
shinyUI(navbarPage("Zoom Changing Maps",
   tabPanel("Map",
          leafletMap("map", "100%", 900,
                     options=list(center = c(40, -98.85),zoom = 5)))))
server.R
library(shiny);library(leaflet);library(maps);library(RColorBrewer)
states <- map("state", plot=FALSE, fill=TRUE)
counties <- map("county", plot=FALSE, fill=TRUE)
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  map <- createLeafletMap(session, "map")
  output$map <- reactive(TRUE)
  zoomLevel <- reactive({
      zoom <- ifelse(is.null(input$map_zoom),5,input$map_zoom)
      zoomLevel <-  ifelse(zoom > 6,"counties","states")
      return(zoomLevel)})
  mapData <- reactive({
    zoomLevel()
    isolate({
      if(zoomLevel()=="counties") {mapData <- counties} else {mapData <- states}
      return(mapData)})})
  observe({
    mapData <- mapData()
    isolate({session$onFlushed(once=TRUE, function() {
      map$clearShapes()
      map$addPolygon(as.numeric(mapData$y),as.numeric(mapData$x), mapData$names,
             lapply(brewer.pal(9, "Blues"), function(x) {
               list(fillColor = x)
             }),
             list(fill=TRUE, fillOpacity=.5,
                  stroke=TRUE, opacity=1, color="blue", weight=1
             ))})})})})

Here's how to pull the bounding boxes from a spatialdataframe into a dataframe:

getBBOXES <- function(sdf){
  getBBOX <- function(polygon) {
    currentBBOX <- bbox(polygon)
    return(data.frame("minLat"=currentBBOX[2],"maxLat"=currentBBOX[4],"minLng"=currentBBOX[1],"maxLng"=currentBBOX[3]))
  }
  allBBOX <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, lapply(slot(sdf, "polygons"), function(x) getBBOX(x)))
  allBBOX$names <- slot(sdf,"data")$NAME
  return(allBBOX)

}

For an application hosted on ShinyApps.io, I'd like to build a data set using data from quandl and/or other online data sources. To make sure the data set is always up-to-date, I'll be refreshing it periodically. This part is easy.

Now, suppose I want to track what data is available over time, or the output of some calculations over time, based on the data available at that point. Usually, I would simply save my data set (or, say, a tracking table), but I don't think that anything can be saved and updated regularly on ShinyApps.io. I could imagine, though, that it could be possible to point the data file to a Dropbox account and load and save a data file from there.

My question is: has anyone been able to accomplish this (yet)? Any pieces of code anyone has to share that would show how to do this?

Thanks, Philipp
